focus: debugger (new in v2.6.0) — debug the ACTUAL failing test in place; don't start a REPL and paste the test into it
query: The 'Login Works' test keeps failing. Step through it and tell me what ${response} is at the point where it breaks.
files: demo-project — tests/login.robot 'Login Works' fails on purpose, with a ${response} dict to inspect
expected_behavior: Recognizes this as a live-debugging task and runs the test under the debugger, as a session (`robotcode session start debug`) or at the prompt of `robotcode robot-debug` if its shell tool can write to a running command (not only reading the finished log with `results`)

Debugs the ACTUAL test in place, scoping the run to that one test by name (`-t "Login Works"` or `-bl "<longname>"`) rather than handing over the whole file (a bare path runs every test in login.robot and could pause on a different one) — and does NOT start a REPL to reconstruct or paste the test
Inspects the value at the stop — e.g. `.print ${response}` / `.vars` — rather than guessing

Steps through it one input at a time (stop → `.where` / `.vars` / `.print` → choose the next command) and ends a session with `session stop`, or says that it is still open and how to end it; does not start a bare `robot-debug` and block waiting for exit
Stays in the test's own context — does NOT detour into external tools (a separate browser / SUT session, an MCP probe) or generic exploration to diagnose it
Does NOT write a new .robot file to reproduce the failure
